The story achieves a remarkably balanced and effective manipulation of time that mirrors its emotional core—the fleeting nature of a temporary intimacy. 

**Compression of time** is used seamlessly to provide context without bogging down the narrative. Five weeks of residency—and the slow accumulation of unspoken feelings—are compressed into a few sharp, observational paragraphs (such as Marian cataloguing the details of Anton's face, or the two-sentence summary of the night of the power cut). Similarly, the story briefly compresses the near future near the end, summarizing the upcoming farewell dinner, the packing of her bags, and the Monday/Tuesday airport departures. This frames the central afternoon as a suspended island of time.

**Stretching of time** is deployed during the pivotal moments on the beach to heighten emotional tension. When Anton opens the wine bottle with his boot, or peels an egg before answering whether they will stay in touch, the narrative slows down to track small physical details and Marian's internal reactions. The climax of their unspoken romance—when Anton puts his sweater around her shoulders and his hands linger at the collar—stretches a few seconds into two paragraphs of sensory detail and retrospective reflection before the moment is broken by the dog. 

Even within the scene at the beach, an hour passes compressed into a few lines of banter while the tide quietly comes in, brilliantly mirroring how the characters themselves lost track of time before being jolted back to reality. Overall, the pacing feels completely natural and enhances the bittersweet mood of the story.
